term: uniform real increment at each past unit step
definition: UniformPastGrowth S now epsilon says S t+epsilon≤S(t+1) for every integer t<now. Its definition alone permits epsilon≤0; PositiveStep epsilon separately means 0<epsilon. Together they require the SAME positive minimum increment at every past unit step. Merely strict growth or a different positive increment at each step does not give this uniform quantifier scope. No time-indexed cause, conservation law or entropy production law is defined.
note: The uniform lower rate over the entire past is a substantive open background restriction. It is stronger than extrapolating positive changes from any finite observed period. The old exact natural-number unit-cost duration result is orientation only, not a theorem consumed by this proof.
